channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Merchants suffered majority of interchange fee losses, CAT says in landmark ruling
item.description: Visa and Mastercard have largely failed to prove that retailers passed on the overcharges from their multilateral interchange fees to consumers, the UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has said in a ruling expected to have wide-ranging ramifications for several ongoing claims.

item.title: FTC appeals against HSR rule defeat
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission has asked the US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit to overturn a lower court’s ruling finding it failed to justify its expansion of merging filing requirements.

item.title: Facing the music: The Tipline for 18 February 2026
item.description: The Department of Justice is still scheduled to perform its Live Nation show next month, just expect a shorter set list. On Wednesday, the US District Court for the Southern District of New York granted Live Nation’s request to trim allegations that it cornered competition for promotion services and fan ticket sales at major concert venues. item.title: In frame: The Briefing for 19 February 2026
item.description: The UK’s competition watchdog today outlined its provisional Phase II concerns with Getty and Shutterstock’s proposed £3 billion deal, warning the transaction could hamper the supply of editorial content to news organisations. However, the parties successfully convinced the agency to provisionally drop Phase I concerns that the tie-up could harm competition for the global supply of stock content. ...

item.title: Aramark seeks extension to challenge CMA deal block after “unfortunate error”
item.description: An offshore catering company has asked the UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal for an extension to challenge an order by the country’s antitrust watchdog unwinding its acquisition of a rival after its lawyers at Simpson Thacher & Bartlett missed the required deadline.

item.title: South Korean president seeks to banish repeat-offender conspirators
item.description: South Korea’s president Lee Jae Myung has called on the country’s regulators to consider “permanently expelling” repeat cartelists from national markets.

item.title: Spreadex challenges CMA’s second unwinding order in Sporting Index acquisition
item.description: Spreadex has urged the UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal to overturn a decision by the country’s antitrust watchdog requiring it to sell Sporting Index’s consumer business, claiming the agency committed several errors in its “irrational” decision.

item.title: How can that be profitable for Frito-Lay?: The Tipline for 19 February 2026
item.description: Retailers accusing Frito-Lay of price discrimination will not have the opportunity to challenge the merits of the promotional payments and discounts offered to supermarket chains. A federal California judge has struck down the case before discovery, finding that a class action is not the appropriate vehicle for a Robinson-Patman case. item.title: Law firm DEI programme suspended amid FTC scrutiny
item.description: An initiative encouraging law firms to interview a diverse talent pool has been suspended after the Federal Trade Commission sent warning letters to many of its participants.

item.title: Practitioners warn against “radical” California bill
item.description: California’s consideration of legislation to expand antitrust liability involving unilateral conduct would deviate from federal law and create uncertainty for local businesses, several competition experts have said.
